solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Certain to include bizarre giant identifying mark

indicators.note: to include means the first word's synonym wraps round the scrambled letters

parts.note: certain means sure

indicators.note: bizarre suggests something strange and twisted, so the word giant is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sure that a weird giant leaves a recognisable mark behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giant' reads as a noun in the surface, but it is only fodder for 'bizarre'; 'to include' sets the scramble within the synonym of 'Certain'.
explanation.definitionFit: A signature is a person's distinctive handwritten name, the mark that identifies who signed.

clue.text: Resign from raising pets, not happy

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the word pets so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: feeling down is feeling not happy

explanation.surface: Someone giving up a hobby of breeding pets, and glum about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns PETS into STEP, read upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To step down from a post is the idiom for leaving or resigning from it.

clue.text: Performance of US serviceman, good

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A display put on by an American soldier who rates as good.
explanation.definitionFit: A gig is a single live show by musicians or comedians, a performance.

clue.text: Furious article on golf railway

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An angry piece of writing about a railway line by a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Furious and angry are synonyms, describing a person full of rage.

clue.text: Student's unusually guarded nature

definitions.note: read as 'Student is'; the definition is the noun student

indicators.note: unusually tells us the letters of guarded nature appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A student whose temperament is unusually defensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Student's' reads as 'Student is', the 's working as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An undergraduate is a university student who has not yet taken a first degree.

clue.text: This guy Sue, uplifted, thanks before Church

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifted lifts the name Sue so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A man and Sue, feeling cheered, say thank you before going to church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifted' turns SUE into EUS, read upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Eustace is a man's first name, so a particular guy, which the clue points to as 'This guy'.

clue.text: Copper, British — he's young

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A British policeman described as youthful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the metal; 'he's young' fits the cub reporter or animal young.
explanation.definitionFit: A cub is a young animal such as a fox or bear, or a novice like a cub reporter.

clue.text: Cleaner brought over the French bronze — a fake

indicators.note: in a down clue brought over puts the cleaner's word above the next piece

parts.note: a char is a British cleaning lady (charwoman)
la is French for the
a tan is a bronze colour of skin

explanation.surface: A cleaner fetched the French bronze, which turns out to be a forgery.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is an old British word for a cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlatan is a fraud who claims skills he lacks, so a fake person.

clue.text: Frank, off to protect learner

indicators.note: to protect means the first word's synonym surrounds the other piece like a guard

parts.note: food that is off has gone bad
L is for learner, as on a British L-plate

explanation.surface: Frank is going away to look after a trainee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name but is the adjective meaning blunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A bald statement is plain and blunt, a frank one without softening.

clue.text: In from France, joke with editor, busy

parts.note: en is the French word for in
a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: Someone arrived from France, joking with an editor, rushed off their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone line or person that is engaged is occupied, so busy.

clue.text: Delay sales booth

definitions.meaning: to delay or play for time
a stand or booth selling goods in a market

explanation.definitionFit: Stall is both a verb for stalling for time and a noun for a market stand.

clue.text: Not bright, extremely dopey, to cross Welsh river!

indicators.note: to cross means the outer letters span across the other piece, which sits between them
extremely means take only the extreme letters of the word

parts.note: the Usk is a river in south Wales

explanation.surface: A dim person, very dozy, wading over a river in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes D and Y from DOPEY; 'to cross' sets them either side of USK.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusky means dim or shadowy, like dusk, so lacking brightness.

clue.text: A pact goes wrong — he's blamed unfairly

indicators.note: goes wrong suggests the letters of a pact goes have gone awry and are rearranged

explanation.surface: An agreement collapses and one man gets the blame for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scapegoat is someone made to carry the blame for others' faults.

clue.text: In truth referring to supporter

parts.note: re means about or referring to, as in a letter heading
an ally is a supporter

explanation.surface: An honest remark about someone who backs you up.
explanation.definitionFit: Really and in truth are both ways of saying actually or genuinely.

clue.text: With a team completely on top? Indeed so, for a change

definitions.text: With a team completely on top?

indicators.note: for a change tells us to alter the order of the letters of Indeed so

explanation.surface: A sports commentator agreeing that, unusually, one team is dominating.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-sided contest is one where a single team dominates; the question mark flags the definition by example.

clue.text: Be wet — then area unfortunately showing effect of climate

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone badly awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An area doomed to be soaked and battered by its climate.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather-beaten describes a face or building worn and marked by long exposure to wind and rain.

clue.text: Poor leaders in his August papers — like every silly season?

indicators.note: leaders in means take the leading letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A sorry figure reading the August papers, full of trivial stories as every year.
explanation.walkthrough: The silly season is the British term for August, when newspapers fill up with trivial stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Hapless means unlucky or unfortunate, as in 'the poor fellow'.

clue.text: Set of buttons important at home

parts.note: key means important, as in a key issue
pad is slang for one's home or flat

explanation.surface: Buttons that matter a lot to someone in their house.
explanation.definitionFit: A keypad is a small panel of push buttons, as on a phone or alarm.

clue.text: Some bikinis and shorts in beach area

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Swimwear and shorts seen on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'in'; 'in' is a link word, since 'in beach area' cannot replace the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The sands are the sandy stretch of a seashore, the beach itself.

clue.text: Wonderful evening meal: one starter of prawns less

indicators.note: less means the named letter is taken away from the meal

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

indicators.note: one starter of means just the first letter of the word, one copy only

explanation.surface: A great dinner, even with one fewer prawn starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one starter of prawns' is P; 'less' takes one P from SUPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is a slightly old-fashioned exclamation meaning excellent or marvellous.

clue.text: Rent but not from Royal Navy

parts.note: to is the opposite of from, so not from gives to

explanation.surface: A sailor's rent paid elsewhere than to the Royal Navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like a payment, but here it is the past participle of rend, meaning ripped.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent, from rend, means torn apart, as in a garment rent in two.

clue.text: Australian individual, a gas!

parts.note: Oz is slang for Australia or Australian
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: An Australian person who is great fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a gas' reads as slang for a laugh, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a form of oxygen with three atoms, a gas found in the upper atmosphere.

clue.text: Indicate approval of a Parish Priest and Archbishop

parts.note: William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I

explanation.surface: A churchgoer showing approval of the local priest and the archbishop.
explanation.walkthrough: Laud is a famous 17th-century Archbishop of Canterbury.
explanation.definitionFit: To applaud is to clap or praise, showing that you approve of something.

clue.text: Part of pay, especially? Yes

indicators.note: part of means the answer is a portion of the letters in the following words

explanation.surface: Asking whether something is part of one's pay in particular, and getting agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Aye is an old or dialect word for yes, used in votes in Parliament.

clue.text: Northeastern team's first score

indicators.note: first means just the opening letter of the word team's

explanation.surface: A northern team's opening goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks like a noun for the result, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To net is to score, putting the ball into the back of the net.

clue.text: One with leading role moved fast to trap a bird

indicators.note: to trap means the first word's synonym encloses the other pieces like a snare

parts.note: sped means moved fast
the rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: A star player rushed out to catch a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A spearhead is the person or group leading an attack or campaign, at the front.
